sanskrit.deva:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana || 1 ||

padaccheda.iast: saṃnyāsasya mahā-bāho tattvam icchāmi veditum tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśi-niṣūdana
padaccheda.deva: संन्यासस्य महा-बाहो तत्त्वम् इच्छामि वेदितुम् त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक् केशि-निषूदन

translations.text: Arjuna said: I wish to know the truth of renunciation, O mighty-armed, and of abandonment, O Hṛṣīkeśa, separately, O slayer of Keśin.

notes: Śaṅkara: this chapter sums up the meaning of the whole Gītā and of the whole Veda; what was taught in all the earlier chapters is found in it. Arjuna asks only about the meanings of the two words saṃnyāsa and tyāga, as distinct from each other. Keśin was a demon in the form of a horse, slain by Vāsudeva.

sanskrit.deva:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ || 2 ||

lines.iast: kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ
lines.deva: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः

padaccheda.iast: kāmyānām karmaṇām nyāsam saṃnyāsam kavayaḥ viduḥ sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam prāhuḥ tyāgam vicakṣaṇāḥ
padaccheda.deva: काम्यानाम् कर्मणाम् न्यासम् संन्यासम् कवयः विदुः सर्व-कर्म-फल-त्यागम् प्राहुः त्यागम् विचक्षणाः

words.meaning: the abandonment of the fruit of all actions

translations.text: The Blessed Lord said: The learned know renunciation as the giving up of actions prompted by desire; the wise declare abandonment to be the abandonment of the fruit of all actions.

notes: Śaṅkara: actions prompted by desire are the Aśvamedha and the like. ‘All actions’ are the obligatory and occasional ones that are being performed; giving up the fruit that would come to oneself from them is tyāga. Either way the two words mean simply ‘giving up’ and do not differ as ‘pot’ and ‘cloth’ do. (Objection) the obligatory actions have no fruit, so how can it be given up? (Reply) the Lord holds that they do bear fruit, as 18.12 shows.

sanskrit.deva:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ |
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare || 3 ||

padaccheda.iast: tyājyam doṣavat iti eke karma prāhuḥ manīṣiṇaḥ yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyam iti ca apare
padaccheda.deva: त्याज्यम् दोषवत् इति एके कर्म प्राहुः मनीषिणः यज्ञ-दान-तपः-कर्म न त्याज्यम् इति च अपरे

words.meaning: the action of sacrifice, giving and austerity

translations.text: Some thinkers declare that action is to be abandoned as an evil; and others, that the action of sacrifice, giving and austerity is not to be abandoned.

notes: Śaṅkara: doṣavat: all action is faulty because it binds; or, it is to be abandoned as a fault such as attachment is. The first view follows the Sāṃkhya outlook.

Śaṅkara: these alternatives concern only those entitled to action. The renouncers established in knowledge are not in question: they see neither bodily pain nor action in the Self, so abandonment from fear of pain or from delusion (18.7–8) cannot apply to them. What is praised here as abandonment of sattva is the giving up of the fruit of action by men of action who do not know the Self; it is called renunciation by way of praise and is not the renunciation of all action in the primary sense. ‘It is not possible for an embodied being’ (18.11) is likewise said in praise. About 160 characters of this long passage were not read.

sanskrit.deva:
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama |
tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ || 4 ||

lines.iast: niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama
lines.deva: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम

padaccheda.iast: niścayam śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama tyāgaḥ hi puruṣa-vyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: निश्चयम् शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरत-सत्तम त्यागः हि पुरुष-व्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Hear my conclusion about that abandonment, O best of the Bharatas. For abandonment, O tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.

notes: Śaṅkara: he says ‘abandonment’ alone, meaning that what the two words tyāga and saṃnyāsa denote is one. It is of three kinds, of tamas and the rest, for the man of action who does not know the Self, and not for one who sees the highest truth. This is hard to know, so no one else can state the truth of it.

sanskrit.deva:
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat |
yajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām || 5 ||

padaccheda.iast: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyam kāryam eva tat yajñaḥ dānam tapaḥ ca eva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
padaccheda.deva: यज्ञ-दान-तपः-कर्म न त्याज्यम् कार्यम् एव तत् यज्ञः दानम् तपः च एव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्

words.meaning: the action of sacrifice, giving and austerity

translations.text: The action of sacrifice, giving and austerity is not to be abandoned; it is indeed to be done. Sacrifice, giving and austerity are purifiers of the wise.

notes: Śaṅkara: of the wise who do not aim at the fruit.

sanskrit.deva:
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam || 6 ||

lines.iast: etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca
lines.deva: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च

padaccheda.iast: etāni api tu karmāṇi saṅgam tyaktvā phalāni ca kartavyāni iti me pārtha niścitam matam uttamam
padaccheda.deva: एतानि अपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गम् त्यक्त्वा फलानि च कर्तव्यानि इति मे पार्थ निश्चितम् मतम् उत्तमम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: But even these actions are to be done abandoning attachment and the fruits: this, O Pārtha, is my settled and highest view.

notes: Śaṅkara: this concludes what was promised in 18.4. ‘Even these’: even these actions, which bind one who is attached and seeks their fruit, are to be done by the seeker of liberation. Others take ‘even these’ to mean actions prompted by desire, on the ground that obligatory actions have no fruit. That is wrong: their fruit has been shown (18.5), and one who wishes to give up even obligatory actions for fear of bondage has nothing to do with actions prompted by desire.

sanskrit.deva:
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते ।
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate |
mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 7 ||

padaccheda.iast: niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇaḥ na upapadyate mohāt tasya parityāgaḥ tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणः न उपपद्यते मोहात् तस्य परित्यागः तामसः परिकीर्तितः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. gen. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: But the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; its abandonment from delusion is declared to be of tamas.

notes: Śaṅkara: for the seeker of liberation who does not know the Self and is entitled to action, since for him it is a purifier. ‘Obligatory’ means that it must be done, and yet it is abandoned: that is a contradiction, so the abandonment comes from delusion, and delusion is tamas.

sanskrit.deva:
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet |
sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet || 8 ||

lines.iast: sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet
lines.deva: स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्

padaccheda.iast: duḥkham iti eva yat karma kāya-kleśa-bhayāt tyajet saḥ kṛtvā rājasam tyāgam na eva tyāga-phalam labhet
padaccheda.deva: दुःखम् इति एव यत् कर्म काय-क्लेश-भयात् त्यजेत् सः कृत्वा राजसम् त्यागम् न एव त्याग-फलम् लभेत्

translations.text: He who abandons an action merely because it is painful, from fear of bodily hardship, makes an abandonment of rajas and would not obtain the fruit of abandonment.

notes: Śaṅkara: the fruit is liberation, the fruit of the abandonment of all action that is preceded by knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन ।
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate 'rjuna |
saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ || 9 ||

lines.iast: saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
lines.deva: सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः

padaccheda.iast: kāryam iti eva yat karma niyatam kriyate arjuna saṅgam tyaktvā phalam ca eva saḥ tyāgaḥ sāttvikaḥ mataḥ
padaccheda.deva: कार्यम् इति एव यत् कर्म नियतम् क्रियते अर्जुन सङ्गम् त्यक्त्वा फलम् च एव सः त्यागः सात्त्विकः मतः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: When an obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, simply because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and the fruit, that abandonment is held to be of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: or, though no fruit of an obligatory action is stated, the man who does not know imagines that it purifies him or wards off the fault of omission; ‘abandoning the fruit’ rules out that fancy too. (Objection) the topic is the threefold giving up of action; how is giving up attachment and fruit the third kind? (Reply) both are alike in being abandonment; by blaming the giving up of action as of rajas and tamas, the giving up of the aim at its fruit is praised as of sattva.

sanskrit.deva:
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate |
tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ || 10 ||

padaccheda.iast: na dveṣṭi akuśalam karma kuśale na anuṣajjate tyāgī sattva-samāviṣṭaḥ medhāvī chinna-saṃśayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: न द्वेष्टि अकुशलम् कर्म कुशले न अनुषज्जते त्यागी सत्त्व-समाविष्टः मेधावी छिन्न-संशयः

translations.text: The abandoner, filled with sattva, wise, his doubts cut, does not hate a disagreeable action, nor is he attached to an agreeable one.

notes: Śaṅkara: the inner organ of one who does obligatory action without attachment and without aim at its fruit grows pure and fit to reflect on the Self; this verse tells how he comes by degrees to be established in knowledge. akuśala is action prompted by desire, a cause of the cycle of birth and death; kuśala is obligatory action, which he does not cling to as ‘the cause of liberation’. sattva is the cause of discerning the Self from what is not the Self; medhā is the wisdom that is knowledge of the Self; the doubt cut is that made by ignorance: he is sure that abiding in the Self's own nature alone is the means to the highest good. Such a man, mentally renouncing all action, reaches steadfastness in knowledge: this is the purpose of the yoga of action.

sanskrit.deva:
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ |
yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate || 11 ||

lines.iast: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ
lines.deva: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः

padaccheda.iast: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyam tyaktum karmāṇi aśeṣataḥ yaḥ tu karma-phala-tyāgī saḥ tyāgī iti abhidhīyate
padaccheda.deva: न हि देहभृता शक्यम् त्यक्तुम् कर्माणि अशेषतः यः तु कर्म-फल-त्यागी सः त्यागी इति अभिधीयते

words.meaning: one who abandons the fruit of action

translations.text: For it is not possible for an embodied being to abandon actions entirely; but he who abandons the fruit of action is called an abandoner.

notes: Śaṅkara: dehabhṛt here is one who takes the body to be the Self, firm in the thought ‘I am the doer’, and not the man of discernment. He cannot give up all action, and is entitled only to do the enjoined actions while abandoning their fruit; he is called an abandoner, though a man of action, by way of praise. So the renunciation of all action is possible only for one who sees the highest truth and does not take the body to be the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit || 12 ||

lines.iast: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
lines.deva: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्

lines.iast: bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit
lines.deva: भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्

padaccheda.iast: aniṣṭam iṣṭam miśram ca trividham karmaṇaḥ phalam bhavati atyāginām pretya na tu saṃnyāsinām kvacit
padaccheda.deva: अनिष्टम् इष्टम् मिश्रम् च त्रिविधम् कर्मणः फलम् भवति अत्यागिनाम् प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनाम् क्वचित्

words.meaning: to those who have not abandoned

translations.text: The threefold fruit of action, unwished-for, wished-for and mixed, comes after death to those who have not abandoned, but never to renouncers.

notes: Śaṅkara: unwished-for: hell, animal birth and the like; wished-for: the state of gods and the like; mixed: human birth. Action is dharma and adharma. Its fruit, made by ignorance, is like a magician's show; phala is so called because, being worthless (phalgu), it vanishes (laya). Those who have not abandoned are men of action, not renouncers in the true sense. The renouncers are the wandering ascetics established in knowledge alone, for right seeing uproots ignorance and the other seeds of the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit.deva:
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।
सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me |
sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām || 13 ||

padaccheda.iast: pañca etāni mahā-bāho kāraṇāni nibodha me sāṃkhye kṛta-ante proktāni siddhaye sarva-karmaṇām
padaccheda.deva: पञ्च एतानि महा-बाहो कारणानि निबोध मे सांख्ये कृत-अन्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्व-कर्मणाम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. pl.

translations.text: Learn from me, O mighty-armed, these five causes for the accomplishment of all actions, taught in the Sāṃkhya, in which action ends.

notes: Śaṅkara: the renunciation of all action is possible only for one who sees the highest truth, since action, its factors and its fruit are superimposed on the Self by ignorance; the following verses show this. sāṃkhya is the śāstra in which the things to be known are enumerated, that is, the Vedānta. kṛtānta qualifies it: kṛta is action, and it is where action comes to its end, for when knowledge of the Self arises all action ceases (2.46, 4.33).

sanskrit.deva:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham |
vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam || 14 ||

lines.iast: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham
lines.deva: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्

padaccheda.iast: adhiṣṭhānam tathā kartā karaṇam ca pṛthagvidham vividhāḥ ca pṛthak ceṣṭāḥ daivam ca eva atra pañcamam
padaccheda.deva: अधिष्ठानम् तथा कर्ता करणम् च पृथग्विधम् विविधाः च पृथक् चेष्टाः दैवम् च एव अत्र पञ्चमम्

translations.text: The seat, the agent, the instruments of various kinds, the manifold distinct motions, and the divine, the fifth among these.

notes: Śaṅkara: the seat is the body, the ground in which desire, aversion, pleasure, pain and knowledge show themselves. The agent is the experiencer marked by his limiting adjuncts. The instruments are hearing and the rest, twelve in number. The motions are those of the breath, the out-breath, in-breath and the rest. The divine is the sun and the other gods who favour the eye and the other organs.

sanskrit.deva:
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः ।
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ |
nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ || 15 ||

lines.iast: nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ
lines.deva: न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः

padaccheda.iast: śarīra-vāk-manobhiḥ yat karma prārabhate naraḥ nyāyyam vā viparītam vā pañca ete tasya hetavaḥ
padaccheda.deva: शरीर-वाक्-मनोभिः यत् कर्म प्रारभते नरः न्याय्यम् वा विपरीतम् वा पञ्च एते तस्य हेतवः

translations.text: Whatever action a man undertakes with body, speech and mind, whether right or the contrary, these five are its causes.

notes: Śaṅkara: right: in accord with dharma and scripture; the contrary: against them. Acts that merely keep one alive, such as blinking, are effects of earlier dharma and adharma and so are included. All action enjoined or forbidden has body, speech or mind as chief, and seeing, hearing and the like are their parts; so it is grouped under these three.

sanskrit.deva:
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ |
paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ || 16 ||

lines.iast: tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ
lines.deva: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः

padaccheda.iast: tatra evam sati kartāram ātmānam kevalam tu yaḥ paśyati akṛta-buddhitvāt na saḥ paśyati durmatiḥ
padaccheda.deva: तत्र एवम् सति कर्तारम् आत्मानम् केवलम् तु यः पश्यति अकृत-बुद्धित्वात् न सः पश्यति दुर्मतिः

translations.text: This being so, he who, because his understanding is untrained, sees the Self, which is alone, as the agent, that man of perverse mind does not see.

notes: Śaṅkara: though action is carried out by these five, imagined through ignorance to be the Self, he thinks ‘I alone am the doer’; kevala is ‘pure’. His understanding is not trained by the Vedānta, a teacher's instruction and reasoning. Even one who holds that the Self is other than the body, yet sees that Self alone as the doer, is of untrained understanding. His mind is perverse, the cause of endless birth and death. He sees and yet does not see, as one with an eye disease sees many moons, or as one thinks the moon runs when the clouds run.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमांल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvāpi sa imāṃllokānna hanti na nibadhyate || 17 ||

lines.iast: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate
lines.deva: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते

lines.iast: hatvāpi sa imāṃllokānna hanti na nibadhyate
lines.deva: हत्वापि स इमांल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते

padaccheda.iast: yasya na ahaṃkṛtaḥ bhāvaḥ buddhiḥ yasya na lipyate hatvā api saḥ imān lokān na hanti na nibadhyate
padaccheda.deva: यस्य न अहंकृतः भावः बुद्धिः यस्य न लिप्यते हत्वा अपि सः इमान् लोकान् न हन्ति न निबध्यते

translations.text: He who has not the notion ‘I am the doer’, whose understanding is not tainted, even though he slays these creatures, does not slay, nor is he bound.

notes: Śaṅkara: he sees: ‘these five, imagined in the Self through ignorance, are the doers of all actions, not I; I am the witness of their working, alone and changeless’. His understanding does not regret: ‘I did this, and by it I shall go to hell’. lokān: all these living beings. ‘Though he slays’ is said from the worldly view, ‘he does not slay’ from the view of the highest truth.

Śaṅkara: nor does the Self act in combination with the five: what is changeless cannot combine with anything, so ‘alone’ (18.16) only restates its nature. That the Self is changeless is taught in the Gītā (2.25, 3.27, 13.31), in śruti and by reasoning. What ignorance brings to it does not belong to it, as silver does not belong to the shell. This closes what was begun at 2.19–21: the knower has no duty of action, and the threefold fruit does not come to renouncers. This is the meaning of the Gītā and the essence of the whole Veda. About 160 characters of this long passage were not read.

sanskrit.deva:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā |
karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ || 18 ||

padaccheda.iast: jñānam jñeyam parijñātā trividhā karma-codanā karaṇam karma kartā iti trividhaḥ karma-saṃgrahaḥ
padaccheda.deva: ज्ञानम् ज्ञेयम् परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्म-चोदना करणम् कर्म कर्ता इति त्रिविधः कर्म-संग्रहः

translations.text: Knowledge, what is to be known and the knower are the threefold prompting to action; the instrument, the object and the agent are the threefold compass of action.

notes: Śaṅkara: knowledge here is knowledge of any object, and what is to be known is any object; the knower is the experiencer imagined through ignorance. When the three meet, action begins, to avoid or to obtain something. The instrument is outer, hearing and the rest, and inner, the understanding and the rest. karma here is what the agent most wants to reach by his act. Action inheres in these three, so they are its compass.

sanskrit.deva:
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ |
procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi || 19 ||

lines.iast: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ
lines.deva: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः

padaccheda.iast: jñānam karma ca kartā ca tridhā eva guṇa-bhedataḥ procyate guṇa-saṃkhyāne yathāvat śṛṇu tāni api
padaccheda.deva: ज्ञानम् कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधा एव गुण-भेदतः प्रोच्यते गुण-संख्याने यथावत् शृणु तानि अपि

words.meaning: according to the difference of the guṇas
in the enumeration of the guṇas

translations.text: Knowledge, action and the agent are declared in the enumeration of the guṇas to be of three kinds only, according to the difference of the guṇas. Hear of them also, duly.

notes: Śaṅkara: karma here is the act, and not the technical ‘object’ of 18.18. ‘Only’: there is no class apart from the guṇas. guṇa-saṃkhyāna is the śāstra of Kapila; though it conflicts with the oneness of Brahman, the highest truth, its followers are expert in the working of the guṇas, and it is cited in support of what follows.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate |
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam || 20 ||

padaccheda.iast: sarva-bhūteṣu yena ekam bhāvam avyayam īkṣate avibhaktam vibhakteṣu tat jñānam viddhi sāttvikam
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-भूतेषु येन एकम् भावम् अव्ययम् ईक्षते अविभक्तम् विभक्तेषु तत् ज्ञानम् विद्धि सात्त्विकम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. loc. pl.

translations.text: That knowledge by which one sees one undecaying reality in all beings, undivided in the divided: know that to be of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: beings from the unmanifest down to the unmoving. bhāva means a thing: the one reality that is the Self, which does not decay either in itself or in its properties. It is not divided in the different bodies, being continuous like space. This is right seeing, whose object is the non-dual Self.

sanskrit.deva:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān |
vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam || 21 ||

lines.iast: vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam
lines.deva: वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्

padaccheda.iast: pṛthaktvena tu yat jñānam nānā-bhāvān pṛthagvidhān vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tat jñānam viddhi rājasam
padaccheda.deva: पृथक्त्वेन तु यत् ज्ञानम् नाना-भावान् पृथग्विधान् वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तत् ज्ञानम् विद्धि राजसम्

translations.text: But that knowledge which knows in all beings different entities of various kinds, as separate: know that knowledge to be of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: the views of duality are not right views; being of rajas and tamas, they do not directly end the cycle of birth and death. This one knows selves as different in each body. Since knowledge cannot be an agent, ‘which knows’ means ‘by which one knows’.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukam |
atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 22 ||

padaccheda.iast: yat tu kṛtsna-vat ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam atattva-arthavat alpam ca tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
padaccheda.deva: यत् तु कृत्स्न-वत् एकस्मिन् कार्ये सक्तम् अहैतुकम् अतत्त्व-अर्थवत् अल्पम् च तत् तामसम् उदाहृतम्

words.meaning: as if it were the whole

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: not having the truth for its object

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: But that which clings to one effect as if it were the whole, without reason, not having the truth for its object, and petty, is declared to be of tamas.

notes: Śaṅkara: the one effect is the body, or an outer thing such as an image: ‘the Self, or the Lord, is just this much and nothing beyond’; as the naked mendicants hold the jīva to be within the body and of its size, or as some take the Lord to be mere stone or wood. It is petty because its object, or its fruit, is small.

sanskrit.deva:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam |
aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate || 23 ||

padaccheda.iast: niyatam saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣataḥ kṛtam aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam ucyate
padaccheda.deva: नियतम् सङ्ग-रहितम् अराग-द्वेषतः कृतम् अफल-प्रेप्सुना कर्म यत् तत् सात्त्विकम् उच्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: by one who does not seek its fruit

translations.text: The action that is obligatory, free from attachment, done without love or hate by one who does not seek its fruit, is called of sattva.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः ।
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ |
kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam || 24 ||

lines.iast: yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ
lines.deva: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः

padaccheda.iast: yat tu kāma-īpsunā karma sa-ahaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ kriyate bahula-āyāsam tat rājasam udāhṛtam
padaccheda.deva: यत् तु काम-ईप्सुना कर्म स-अहंकारेण वा पुनः क्रियते बहुल-आयासम् तत् राजसम् उदाहृतम्

words.meaning: by one who seeks what he desires
by one with the sense of ‘I’

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: But the action that is done by one who seeks what he desires, or by one with the sense of ‘I’, with much toil, is declared to be of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: kāmepsu: seeking the fruit of the action. ‘With the sense of ‘I’’ is said in contrast with a learned man of the world who is called free of it, and not in contrast with the knower of the truth; for even the doer of an action of sattva, if he does not know the Self, has the sense of ‘I’. punaḥ only fills the line.

sanskrit.deva:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsām anapekṣya ca pauruṣam |
mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate || 25 ||

lines.iast: anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsām anapekṣya ca pauruṣam

padaccheda.iast: anubandham kṣayam hiṃsām anapekṣya ca pauruṣam mohāt ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam ucyate
padaccheda.deva: अनुबन्धम् क्षयम् हिंसाम् अनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् मोहात् आरभ्यते कर्म यत् तत् तामसम् उच्यते

translations.text: The action that is undertaken from delusion, without regard to the consequence, loss, injury and one's own ability, is called of tamas.

notes: Śaṅkara: loss of strength or of wealth; injury to living beings; ability: ‘I am able to finish this action’.

sanskrit.deva:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
muktasaṅgo 'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ |
siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate || 26 ||

padaccheda.iast: mukta-saṅgaḥ anahaṃvādī dhṛti-utsāha-samanvitaḥ siddhi-asiddhyoḥ nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvikaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: मुक्त-सङ्गः अनहंवादी धृति-उत्साह-समन्वितः सिद्धि-असिद्ध्योः निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विकः उच्यते

translations.text: The agent who is free from attachment, not given to speaking of ‘I’, endowed with firmness and zeal, unchanged in success and failure, is called of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: unchanged: moved to act only by the authority of scripture, and not by desire for the fruit and the like.

sanskrit.deva:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako 'śuciḥ |
harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 27 ||

padaccheda.iast: rāgī karma-phala-prepsuḥ lubdhaḥ hiṃsā-ātmakaḥ aśuciḥ harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: रागी कर्म-फल-प्रेप्सुः लुब्धः हिंसा-आत्मकः अशुचिः हर्ष-शोक-अन्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: The agent who is passionate, seeking the fruit of action, greedy, given to injury, impure, subject to joy and grief, is declared to be of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: greedy: thirsting for what belongs to others, or not parting with his own at holy places and the like. Joy at gaining the wished-for, grief at meeting the unwished-for or losing the wished-for; or at the success and failure of that very action.

sanskrit.deva:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैकृतिकोऽलसः ।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naikṛtiko 'lasaḥ |
viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate || 28 ||

lines.iast: viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate
lines.deva: विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭhaḥ naikṛtikaḥ alasaḥ viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठः नैकृतिकः अलसः विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामसः उच्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: The agent who is uncollected, uncultivated, unbending, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is called of tamas.

notes: Śaṅkara: prākṛta: of wholly untrained understanding, like a child. Unbending: like a staff, he bows to no one. śaṭha: he hides what he can do. naikṛtika: intent on setting others at odds. dīrghasūtrin: what should be done today or tomorrow he does not do even in a month.

sanskrit.deva:
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनंजय ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya || 29 ||

padaccheda.iast: buddheḥ bhedam dhṛteḥ ca eva guṇataḥ trividham śṛṇu procyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya
padaccheda.deva: बुद्धेः भेदम् धृतेः च एव गुणतः त्रिविधम् शृणु प्रोच्यमानम् अशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनंजय

translations.text: Hear the threefold division of understanding and of firmness according to the guṇas, declared in full and severally, O winner of wealth.

notes: Śaṅkara: Arjuna is Dhanaṃjaya because in his conquest of the quarters he won much wealth, human and divine.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 30 ||

lines.iast: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye
lines.deva: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये

lines.iast: bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
lines.deva: बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी

padaccheda.iast: pravṛttim ca nivṛttim ca kārya-akārye bhaya-abhaye bandham mokṣam ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
padaccheda.deva: प्रवृत्तिम् च निवृत्तिम् च कार्य-अकार्ये भय-अभये बन्धम् मोक्षम् च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी

words.meaning: what is and is not to be done

translations.text: The understanding that knows the path of action and the path of renunciation, what is and is not to be done, fear and freedom from fear, bondage and liberation, O Pārtha, is of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: since they stand in one sentence with bondage and liberation, pravṛtti is the path of action, the cause of bondage, and nivṛtti the path of renunciation, the cause of liberation. Fear and its absence mean their causes, seen and unseen. Bondage and liberation are known together with their causes. Knowledge is a state of the understanding; firmness too is a particular state of it.

sanskrit.deva:
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca |
ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 31 ||

lines.iast: yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca
lines.deva: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च

padaccheda.iast: yayā dharmam adharmam ca kāryam ca akāryam eva ca ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
padaccheda.deva: यया धर्मम् अधर्मम् च कार्यम् च अकार्यम् एव च अयथावत् प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी

words.meaning: what is not to be done

translations.text: The understanding by which one understands dharma and adharma, what is to be done and what is not to be done, not as they are, O Pārtha, is of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: dharma is what scripture enjoins, adharma what it forbids. ‘Not as they are’: not with certainty in every respect.

sanskrit.deva:
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता ।
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā |
sarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 32 ||

padaccheda.iast: adharmam dharmam iti yā manyate tamasā āvṛtā sarva-arthān viparītān ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
padaccheda.deva: अधर्मम् धर्मम् इति या मन्यते तमसा आवृता सर्व-अर्थान् विपरीतान् च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: The understanding which, covered by darkness, thinks adharma to be dharma, and all things the wrong way round, O Pārtha, is of tamas.

sanskrit.deva:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ |
yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 33 ||

padaccheda.iast: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥ-prāṇa-indriya-kriyāḥ yogena avyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
padaccheda.deva: धृत्या यया धारयते मनः-प्राण-इन्द्रिय-क्रियाः योगेन अव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी

words.meaning: the workings of mind, breath and senses

translations.text: The unswerving firmness by which, through concentration, one holds the workings of mind, breath and senses, O Pārtha, is of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘unswerving’ goes with ‘firmness’. It holds them back from the path that scripture forbids. yoga is samādhi: the firmness is always accompanied by concentration.

sanskrit.deva:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन ।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yayā tu dharmakāmārthāndhṛtyā dhārayate 'rjuna |
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 34 ||

lines.iast: prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
lines.deva: प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी

padaccheda.iast: yayā tu dharma-kāma-arthān dhṛtyā dhārayate arjuna prasaṅgena phala-ākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
padaccheda.deva: यया तु धर्म-काम-अर्थान् धृत्या धारयते अर्जुन प्रसङ्गेन फल-आकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी

words.meaning: one who longs for their fruit

translations.text: But the firmness by which one holds to dharma, pleasure and wealth, O Arjuna, longing for their fruit as the occasion arises, O Pārtha, is of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: he keeps them fixed in mind as things always to be done, and, as each comes up, longs for its fruit.

sanskrit.deva:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 35 ||

lines.iast: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca
lines.deva: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च

lines.iast: na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
lines.deva: न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी

padaccheda.iast: yayā svapnam bhayam śokam viṣādam madam eva ca na vimuñcati durmedhāḥ dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
padaccheda.deva: यया स्वप्नम् भयम् शोकम् विषादम् मदम् एव च न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधाः धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी

translations.text: The firmness by which a man of poor understanding does not give up sleep, fear, grief, despondency and intoxication, O Pārtha, is of tamas.

notes: Śaṅkara: mada: thinking much of indulgence in sense objects, like one drunk. Śaṅkara's text ends the verse sā tāmasī matā, ‘is held to be of tamas’; the reading here is that of the source.

sanskrit.deva:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥ ३६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati || 36 ||

lines.iast: sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha
lines.deva: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ

padaccheda.iast: sukham tu idānīm trividham śṛṇu me bharata-ṛṣabha abhyāsāt ramate yatra duḥkha-antam ca nigacchati
padaccheda.deva: सुखम् तु इदानीम् त्रिविधम् शृणु मे भरत-ऋषभ अभ्यासात् रमते यत्र दुःख-अन्तम् च निगच्छति

translations.text: But now hear from me, O best of the Bharatas, of happiness of three kinds: that in which one delights through practice and reaches the end of pain;

notes: Śaṅkara: the threefold division of acts and of the factors of action has been told; now that of their fruit, happiness. Practice is familiarity, repetition.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥ ३७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam |
tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam || 37 ||

padaccheda.iast: yat tat agre viṣam iva pariṇāme amṛta-upamam tat sukham sāttvikam proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam
padaccheda.deva: यत् तत् अग्रे विषम् इव परिणामे अमृत-उपमम् तत् सुखम् सात्त्विकम् प्रोक्तम् आत्म-बुद्धि-प्रसाद-जम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: born of the clearness of one's understanding

translations.text: which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end: that happiness, born of the clearness of one's understanding, is said to be of sattva.

notes: Śaṅkara: at first, when knowledge, dispassion, meditation and concentration are begun, it is painful because of the great effort; in the end it is the happiness born of their ripening. prasāda is clearness, like that of water. Or ātma-buddhi is the understanding that has the Self for its object.

sanskrit.deva:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre 'mṛtopamam |
pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam || 38 ||

padaccheda.iast: viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogāt yat tat agre amṛta-upamam pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukham rājasam smṛtam
padaccheda.deva: विषय-इन्द्रिय-संयोगात् यत् तत् अग्रे अमृत-उपमम् परिणामे विषम् इव तत् सुखम् राजसम् स्मृतम्

words.meaning: from the contact of senses and objects

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: That happiness which comes from the contact of senses and objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is held to be of rajas.

notes: Śaṅkara: like poison in the end, because it causes loss of strength, vigour, beauty, wisdom, memory, wealth and energy, and because it leads to adharma and to the hell born of it.

sanskrit.deva:
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ ३९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ |
nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 39 ||

padaccheda.iast: yat agre ca anubandhe ca sukham mohanam ātmanaḥ nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-uttham tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
padaccheda.deva: यत् अग्रे च अनुबन्धे च सुखम् मोहनम् आत्मनः निद्रा-आलस्य-प्रमाद-उत्थम् तत् तामसम् उदाहृतम्

words.meaning: arising from sleep, laziness and negligence

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: That happiness which deludes oneself both at first and in its sequel, arising from sleep, laziness and negligence, is declared to be of tamas.

sanskrit.deva:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥ ४० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ |
sattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ || 40 ||

lines.iast: na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ
lines.deva: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः

padaccheda.iast: na tat asti pṛthivyām vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ sattvam prakṛti-jaiḥ muktam yat ebhiḥ syāt tribhiḥ guṇaiḥ
padaccheda.deva: न तत् अस्ति पृथिव्याम् वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः सत्त्वम् प्रकृति-जैः मुक्तम् यत् एभिः स्यात् त्रिभिः गुणैः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: There is no being on earth, or again in heaven among the gods, that is free from these three guṇas born of Prakṛti.

notes: Śaṅkara: this verse closes the topic. sattva here is a living creature, or any other thing without life.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप ।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥ ४१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ || 41 ||

padaccheda.iast: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśām śūdrāṇām ca paraṃtapa karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ guṇaiḥ
padaccheda.deva: ब्राह्मण-क्षत्रिय-विशाम् शूद्राणाम् च परंतप कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभाव-प्रभवैः गुणैः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. pl.

translations.text: The actions of brāhmaṇas, warriors and traders, and of servants, O scorcher of foes, are divided by the guṇas arising from their own nature.

notes: Śaṅkara: the whole cycle of birth and death, made of the three guṇas and imagined through ignorance, has been described, and the tree is to be cut (15.1–4). Since everything is made of the guṇas, how its cause may cease has now to be told, and the meaning of the whole Gītā summed up. The śūdras are named apart because, being of one birth, they are not entitled to the Veda.

Śaṅkara: svabhāva is the Lord's Prakṛti, the illusion made of the three guṇas. Or: sattva is the source of the brāhmaṇa's nature; rajas with sattva subordinate, of the warrior's; rajas with tamas subordinate, of the trader's; tamas with rajas subordinate, of the servant's. Or: svabhāva is the impression made in other births, showing itself in this one. Scripture too assigns these actions with regard to the guṇas.

sanskrit.deva:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam || 42 ||

padaccheda.iast: śamaḥ damaḥ tapaḥ śaucam kṣāntiḥ ārjavam eva ca jñānam vijñānam āstikyam brahma-karma svabhāva-jam
padaccheda.deva: शमः दमः तपः शौचम् क्षान्तिः आर्जवम् एव च ज्ञानम् विज्ञानम् आस्तिक्यम् ब्रह्म-कर्म स्वभाव-जम्

translations.text: Calm, restraint of the senses, austerity, purity, forbearance, uprightness, knowledge, realization and faith are the action of a brāhmaṇa, born of his own nature.

notes: Śaṅkara: āstikya is trust in what the scriptures teach. ‘Born of his own nature’ repeats ‘divided by the guṇas arising from their own nature’.

sanskrit.deva:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षत्रकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣatrakarma svabhāvajam || 43 ||

padaccheda.iast: śauryam tejaḥ dhṛtiḥ dākṣyam yuddhe ca api apalāyanam dānam īśvara-bhāvaḥ ca kṣatra-karma svabhāva-jam
padaccheda.deva: शौर्यम् तेजः धृतिः दाक्ष्यम् युद्धे च अपि अपलायनम् दानम् ईश्वर-भावः च क्षत्र-कर्म स्वभाव-जम्

translations.text: Valour, boldness, firmness, skill, not fleeing in battle, giving and lordliness are the action of a warrior, born of his own nature.

notes: Śaṅkara: skill is acting without confusion in duties that arise suddenly. Giving is open-handedness. Lordliness is showing the power of a ruler towards those to be ruled.

sanskrit.deva:
कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥ ४४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam || 44 ||

padaccheda.iast: kṛṣi-gorakṣya-vāṇijyam vaiśya-karma svabhāva-jam paricaryā-ātmakam karma śūdrasya api svabhāva-jam
padaccheda.deva: कृषि-गोरक्ष्य-वाणिज्यम् वैश्य-कर्म स्वभाव-जम् परिचर्या-आत्मकम् कर्म शूद्रस्य अपि स्वभाव-जम्

translations.text: Ploughing, cattle-keeping and trade are the action of a trader, born of his own nature; and action consisting of service is that of a servant, born of his own nature.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥ ४५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu || 45 ||

lines.iast: sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ
lines.deva: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः

padaccheda.iast: sve sve karmaṇi abhirataḥ saṃsiddhim labhate naraḥ sva-karma-nirataḥ siddhim yathā vindati tat śṛṇu
padaccheda.deva: स्वे स्वे कर्मणि अभिरतः संसिद्धिम् लभते नरः स्व-कर्म-निरतः सिद्धिम् यथा विन्दति तत् शृणु

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: one intent on his own action

translations.text: Devoted each to his own action, a man attains perfection. Hear how one intent on his own action finds perfection.

notes: Śaṅkara: the natural fruit of these actions, rightly done, is heaven, as the smṛtis say; the fruit now stated comes from another cause. Perfection here is the fitness of body and senses for steadfastness in knowledge, once impurity has worn away through doing one's own action. It does not come directly from the action alone; how it comes is told next.

sanskrit.deva:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥ ४६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ || 46 ||

padaccheda.iast: yataḥ pravṛttiḥ bhūtānām yena sarvam idam tatam sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhim vindati mānavaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यतः प्रवृत्तिः भूतानाम् येन सर्वम् इदम् ततम् स्व-कर्मणा तम् अभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिम् विन्दति मानवः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: By worshipping with his own action him from whom beings have their origin and by whom all this is pervaded, a man finds perfection.

notes: Śaṅkara: pravṛtti is origin, or activity; he is the Lord, the inner ruler. The perfection is only fitness for steadfastness in knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 47 ||

padaccheda.iast: śreyān svadharmaḥ viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt su-anuṣṭhitāt svabhāva-niyatam karma kurvan na āpnoti kilbiṣam
padaccheda.deva: श्रेयान् स्वधर्मः विगुणः पर-धर्मात् सु-अनुष्ठितात् स्वभाव-नियतम् कर्म कुर्वन् न आप्नोति किल्बिषम्

translations.text: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed. Doing the action ordained by one's own nature, one incurs no sin.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘though’ is to be supplied. As poison does no harm to a worm born in poison, so one who does the action ordained by his nature incurs no sin.

sanskrit.deva:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥ ४८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ || 48 ||

lines.iast: sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet
lines.deva: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्

padaccheda.iast: sahajam karma kaunteya sa-doṣam api na tyajet sarva-ārambhāḥ hi doṣeṇa dhūmena agniḥ iva āvṛtāḥ
padaccheda.deva: सहजम् कर्म कौन्तेय स-दोषम् अपि न त्यजेत् सर्व-आरम्भाः हि दोषेण धूमेन अग्निः इव आवृताः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: One should not abandon the action born with oneself, O son of Kuntī, though it is faulty; for all undertakings are covered by fault, as fire by smoke.

notes: Śaṅkara: all actions, one's own dharma and another's, are faulty because they are made of the three guṇas. By giving up one's own and taking up another's one is not freed from fault; and one who does not know the Self cannot give up action entirely.

Śaṅkara: he then asks whether action cannot be wholly given up because the Puruṣa is ever in motion, like the guṇas of the Sāṃkhyas, or because act and agent are one, like the momentary aggregates of the Buddhists; and he takes up the view of the followers of Kaṇāda, that action arises in and passes from a lasting substance. That view is not the Lord's (2.16), since it holds that the non-existent comes to be and the existent ceases. He concludes: action, a property of the guṇas, is superimposed on the changeless Self by ignorance; so the ignorant man cannot give it up wholly even for a moment (3.5), while the knower, his ignorance removed by knowledge, can, as nothing is left of a second moon when the eye disease is gone. About 2,400 characters in the middle of this passage, the refutation in detail, were not read.

sanskrit.deva:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥ ४९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati || 49 ||

padaccheda.iast: asakta-buddhiḥ sarvatra jita-ātmā vigata-spṛhaḥ naiṣkarmya-siddhim paramām saṃnyāsena adhigacchati
padaccheda.deva: असक्त-बुद्धिः सर्वत्र जित-आत्मा विगत-स्पृहः नैष्कर्म्य-सिद्धिम् परमाम् संन्यासेन अधिगच्छति

translations.text: With understanding unattached everywhere, with mind subdued, free from longing, he attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness.

notes: Śaṅkara: the perfection born of action was fitness for steadfastness in knowledge; this is its fruit. buddhi and ātman are both the inner organ; ‘everywhere’: in sons, wife and other grounds of attachment. naiṣkarmya is the state of one from whom actions have fallen away through knowing the actionless Brahman as his Self; or the perfection is abiding as the actionless Self. It is the state of immediate liberation. saṃnyāsa here is right seeing, or the renunciation of all action that follows on it (5.13).

sanskrit.deva:
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥ ५० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me |
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā || 50 ||

lines.iast: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me
lines.deva: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे

lines.iast: samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
lines.deva: समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा

padaccheda.iast: siddhim prāptaḥ yathā brahma tathā āpnoti nibodha me samāsena eva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
padaccheda.deva: सिद्धिम् प्राप्तः यथा ब्रह्म तथा आप्नोति निबोध मे समासेन एव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Learn from me in brief, O son of Kuntī, how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman, which is the supreme culmination of knowledge.

notes: Śaṅkara: the perfection attained is the fitness for knowledge born of the Lord's grace; Brahman is the supreme Self. niṣṭhā is the culmination, the final end, of the knowledge of Brahman.

Śaṅkara: (objection) knowledge takes the form of its object, and the Self is neither an object nor possessed of form. (Reply) the understanding, being as clear and subtle as the Self, bears a reflection of the Self's consciousness; the mind reflects the understanding, the senses the mind, the body the senses, which is why ordinary people take the body to be the Self. Knowledge is wholly evident, like pleasure, and so is the knower; no effort is needed to gain knowledge, but only to stop taking what is not the Self to be the Self. So steadfastness in knowledge is easy to achieve. About 1,700 characters in the middle of this passage were not read.

sanskrit.deva:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥ ५१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca || 51 ||

lines.iast: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca
lines.deva: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च

padaccheda.iast: buddhyā viśuddhayā yuktaḥ dhṛtyā ātmānam niyamya ca śabda-ādīn viṣayān tyaktvā rāga-dveṣau vyudasya ca
padaccheda.deva: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तः धृत्या आत्मानम् नियम्य च शब्द-आदीन् विषयान् त्यक्त्वा राग-द्वेषौ व्युदस्य च

grammar.en: past passive participle f. ins. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Endowed with a purified understanding, restraining body and organs with firmness, abandoning sound and the other objects, and casting aside love and hate;

notes: Śaṅkara: purified: free of deceit. ātman is the aggregate of body and organs. He gives up all objects beyond what merely keeps the body alive, and gives up love and hate even for those.

sanskrit.deva:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥ ५२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ || 52 ||

padaccheda.iast: vivikta-sevī laghu-āśī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ nityam vairāgyam samupāśritaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विविक्त-सेवी लघु-आशी यत-वाक्-काय-मानसः ध्यान-योग-परः नित्यम् वैराग्यम् समुपाश्रितः

words.meaning: with speech, body and mind controlled

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: resorting to solitude, eating little, with speech, body and mind controlled, always intent on meditation and concentration, having resorted to dispassion;

notes: Śaṅkara: solitary places are a forest, a river bank, a mountain cave. Solitude and light eating are named because they remove sleep and other faults and so clear the mind. dhyāna is thinking on the nature of the Self; yoga is making the mind one-pointed on the Self. ‘Always’ shows that he has no other duty, such as repeating mantras. Dispassion is freedom from thirst for objects seen and unseen.

sanskrit.deva:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ ५३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate || 53 ||

lines.iast: ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham
lines.deva: अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्

padaccheda.iast: ahaṃkāram balam darpam kāmam krodham parigraham vimucya nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ brahma-bhūyāya kalpate
padaccheda.deva: अहंकारम् बलम् दर्पम् कामम् क्रोधम् परिग्रहम् विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तः ब्रह्म-भूयाय कल्पते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: having given up the sense of ‘I’, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, without the sense of ‘mine’ and at peace, he is fit for becoming Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: the sense of ‘I’ in the body and the rest. Force is power joined with desire and passion, and not the natural strength of the body, which cannot be given up. Arrogance follows on elation and leads one to overstep dharma. Even after the faults of senses and mind are given up, outer possessions may come for keeping the body alive or for the practice of dharma; these too he gives up and becomes a wandering renouncer, without ‘mine’ even towards the bare life of the body.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥ ५४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām || 54 ||

lines.iast: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati
lines.deva: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति

lines.iast: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām
lines.deva: समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्

padaccheda.iast: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mat-bhaktim labhate parām
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्म-भूतः प्रसन्न-आत्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मत्-भक्तिम् लभते पराम्

translations.text: Having become Brahman, serene in mind, he neither grieves nor longs. The same towards all beings, he attains supreme devotion to me.

notes: Śaṅkara: he does not grieve over any lack or defect in himself, and a knower of Brahman cannot long for what he has not; this states his nature. Another reading is na hṛṣyati, ‘he does not exult’. ‘The same’: he sees the pleasure and pain of all beings as like his own; the seeing of the Self as the same is not meant here, as it comes in the next verse. The supreme devotion is the fourth, which is knowledge (7.16–18).

sanskrit.deva:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ |
tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram || 55 ||

lines.iast: tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram
lines.deva: ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्

padaccheda.iast: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaḥ ca asmi tattvataḥ tataḥ mām tattvataḥ jñātvā viśate tat-anantaram
padaccheda.deva: भक्त्या माम् अभिजानाति यावान् यः च अस्मि तत्त्वतः ततः माम् तत्त्वतः ज्ञात्वा विशते तत्-अनन्तरम्

translations.text: By devotion he knows me in truth, how great I am and who I am. Then, having known me in truth, he enters into me immediately after that.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘how great’: with the differences of extent made by limiting adjuncts; ‘who’: the supreme Puruṣa free of all such differences, like space, non-dual, pure consciousness. Knowing and entering are not two acts; there is no fruit other than the knowledge itself (13.2).

Śaṅkara: (objection) one knows a thing the moment knowledge of it arises, so how is he said to know by the culmination of knowledge? (Reply) niṣṭhā is knowledge ending in the sure experience of the Self, once its aids are present and what opposes it is absent: the knowledge that the knower of the field and the supreme Self are one, born of scripture and teacher, together with the renunciation of all action. This is the fourth, supreme devotion. All the scriptures that enjoin withdrawal have their purpose here. Steadfastness in knowledge cannot go together with action, as one going to the eastern sea cannot share a road with one going to the western; so it is to be practised only with the renunciation of all action.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥ ५६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ |
matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam || 56 ||

padaccheda.iast: sarva-karmāṇi api sadā kurvāṇaḥ mat-vyapāśrayaḥ mat-prasādāt avāpnoti śāśvatam padam avyayam
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-कर्माणि अपि सदा कुर्वाणः मत्-व्यपाश्रयः मत्-प्रसादात् अवाप्नोति शाश्वतम् पदम् अव्ययम्

translations.text: Even though always doing all actions, one whose refuge I am attains by my grace the eternal, undecaying abode.

notes: Śaṅkara: the yoga of devotion, the worship of the Lord by one's own action, is now praised; its fruit is the fitness for steadfastness in knowledge, which ends in liberation. ‘All actions’: even forbidden ones. The abode is that of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit.deva:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥ ५७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava || 57 ||

padaccheda.iast: cetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-paraḥ buddhi-yogam upāśritya mat-cittaḥ satatam bhava
padaccheda.deva: चेतसा सर्व-कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्-परः बुद्धि-योगम् उपाश्रित्य मत्-चित्तः सततम् भव

translations.text: Giving over all actions to me with the mind, holding me as the supreme, and resorting to the yoga of understanding, always have your mind on me.

notes: Śaṅkara: with the mind: with a discerning understanding; actions with seen and unseen ends are given over to the Lord in the way taught at 9.27. buddhi-yoga is a collected understanding. He reads apāśritya: taking it as one's only refuge.

sanskrit.deva:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहंकारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥ ५८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṃkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi || 58 ||

padaccheda.iast: mat-cittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣyasi atha cet tvam ahaṃkārāt na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi
padaccheda.deva: मत्-चित्तः सर्व-दुर्गाणि मत्-प्रसादात् तरिष्यसि अथ चेत् त्वम् अहंकारात् न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि

translations.text: With your mind on me, you will cross all difficulties by my grace. But if, from the sense of ‘I’, you will not listen, you will perish.

notes: Śaṅkara: the difficulties are the causes of the cycle of birth and death, hard to cross. The sense of ‘I’ here: ‘I am learned’.

sanskrit.deva:
यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥ ५९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadahaṃkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati || 59 ||

padaccheda.iast: yat ahaṃkāram āśritya na yotsye iti manyase mithyā eṣaḥ vyavasāyaḥ te prakṛtiḥ tvām niyokṣyati
padaccheda.deva: यत् अहंकारम् आश्रित्य न योत्स्ये इति मन्यसे मिथ्या एषः व्यवसायः ते प्रकृतिः त्वाम् नियोक्ष्यति

translations.text: If, resorting to the sense of ‘I’, you think ‘I will not fight’, this resolve of yours is vain: your nature will compel you.

notes: Śaṅkara: do not think ‘I am independent; why should I do what another says?’ prakṛti here is the nature of a warrior. He reads yady ahaṃkāram, ‘if’; the source has yad ahaṃkāram.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥ ६० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo 'pi tat || 60 ||

padaccheda.iast: svabhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā kartum na icchasi yat mohāt kariṣyasi avaśaḥ api tat
padaccheda.deva: स्वभाव-जेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा कर्तुम् न इच्छसि यत् मोहात् करिष्यसि अवशः अपि तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Bound by your own action, born of your nature, O son of Kuntī, what from delusion you do not wish to do, that you will do even helplessly.

notes: Śaṅkara: the action born of his nature is valour and the rest (18.43).

sanskrit.deva:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ ६१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā || 61 ||

padaccheda.iast: īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānām hṛt-deśe arjuna tiṣṭhati bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā
padaccheda.deva: ईश्वरः सर्व-भूतानाम् हृत्-देशे अर्जुन तिष्ठति भ्रामयन् सर्व-भूतानि यन्त्र-आरूढानि मायया

words.meaning: in the region of the heart

translations.text: The Lord dwells in the region of the heart of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to revolve by illusion, as if mounted on a machine.

notes: Śaṅkara: the Lord is Nārāyaṇa, whose nature it is to rule. ‘Arjuna’ means of a white, that is, pure inner nature. ‘As if’ is to be supplied: like wooden figures mounted on a machine. māyā here is deception.

sanskrit.deva:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥ ६२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam || 62 ||

padaccheda.iast: tam eva śaraṇam gaccha sarva-bhāvena bhārata tat-prasādāt parām śāntim sthānam prāpsyasi śāśvatam
padaccheda.deva: तम् एव शरणम् गच्छ सर्व-भावेन भारत तत्-प्रसादात् पराम् शान्तिम् स्थानम् प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्

translations.text: Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, O descendant of Bharata. By his grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

notes: Śaṅkara: refuge, to remove the distress of the cycle of birth and death. Peace is cessation; the abode is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit.deva:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥ ६३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru || 63 ||

padaccheda.iast: iti te jñānam ākhyātam guhyāt guhyataram mayā vimṛśya etat aśeṣeṇa yathā icchasi tathā kuru
padaccheda.deva: इति ते ज्ञानम् आख्यातम् गुह्यात् गुह्यतरम् मया विमृश्य एतत् अशेषेण यथा इच्छसि तथा कुरु

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Thus knowledge more secret than the secret has been declared to you by me. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.

notes: Śaṅkara: declared by me, the all-knowing Lord. ‘This’ is the teaching as given, and all that it has said.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥ ६४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam || 64 ||

lines.iast: sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ
lines.deva: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः

lines.iast: iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
lines.deva: इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्

padaccheda.iast: sarva-guhyatamam bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramam vacaḥ iṣṭaḥ asi me dṛḍham iti tataḥ vakṣyāmi te hitam
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-गुह्यतमम् भूयः शृणु मे परमम् वचः इष्टः असि मे दृढम् इति ततः वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are firmly dear to me; therefore I shall tell you what is for your good.

notes: Śaṅkara: though said more than once. ‘Not from fear nor for gain do I speak, but because you are dear to me.’ The good is the means of gaining knowledge, the best of all goods.

sanskrit.deva:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥ ६५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo 'si me || 65 ||

lines.iast: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru
lines.deva: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु

lines.iast: māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo 'si me
lines.deva: मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे

padaccheda.iast: mat-manāḥ bhava mat-bhaktaḥ mat-yājī mām namaskuru mām eva eṣyasi satyam te pratijāne priyaḥ asi me
padaccheda.deva: मत्-मनाः भव मत्-भक्तः मत्-याजी माम् नमस्कुरु माम् एव एष्यसि सत्यम् ते प्रतिजाने प्रियः असि मे

translations.text: Have your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow down to me. You will come to me alone; truly I promise you, for you are dear to me.

notes: Śaṅkara: living so, with end, means and purpose all given over to Vāsudeva. Knowing that the Lord's promise is true and that liberation is the sure fruit of devotion to him, one should have him as one's only refuge: this is the meaning of the sentence.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥ ६६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ || 66 ||

lines.iast: ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
lines.deva: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः

padaccheda.iast: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekam śaraṇam vraja aham tvā sarva-pāpebhyaḥ mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-धर्मान् परित्यज्य माम् एकम् शरणम् व्रज अहम् त्वा सर्व-पापेभ्यः मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः

translations.text: Giving up all dharmas, come to me alone as refuge. I shall free you from all sins; do not grieve.

notes: Śaṅkara: having summed up refuge in the Lord, the highest secret of the path of the yoga of action, he now states its fruit, right seeing, taught as the essence of all the Upaniṣads. ‘Dharma’ here includes adharma too, since actionlessness is meant: giving up all dharmas is renouncing all actions. ‘Me alone’: the Self of all, the same in all beings, the Lord, free from birth, old age and death; know that ‘I am he’ and that there is nothing other than me. The sins are all the bonds of dharma and adharma; he frees by making one's own nature as the Self manifest (10.11).

Śaṅkara then examines at length whether in the Gītā the means to the highest good is knowledge, action, or both together. His conclusion: knowledge of the Self alone, since it removes the notion of difference, of act, agent and fruit, which ignorance has set up in the Self from time without beginning; liberation, being eternal, is not something produced by action, nor by knowledge and action combined. The passage ends: the Self does not truly act or experience through the working of body and organs; the cycle of birth and death is an error resting on a false notion, as in a dream, and it ceases wholly through right seeing. Of this passage of some 15,000 characters only the opening and the close were read; about 12,700 characters of the argument in between were not.

sanskrit.deva:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥ ६७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana |
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati || 67 ||

lines.iast: na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati
lines.deva: न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति

padaccheda.iast: idam te na atapaskāya na abhaktāya kadācana na ca aśuśrūṣave vācyam na ca mām yaḥ abhyasūyati
padaccheda.deva: इदम् ते न अतपस्काय न अभक्ताय कदाचन न च अशुश्रूषवे वाच्यम् न च माम् यः अभ्यसूयति

words.meaning: to one who does not wish to hear

translations.text: This is never to be told by you to one without austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one who does not wish to hear, nor to one who finds fault with me.

notes: Śaṅkara: having summed up the teaching, he gives the rule for handing it on. He takes te as ‘for your good’: this teaching was told for your good. ‘Without devotion’: to teacher and God. Finding fault with me: taking Vāsudeva for an ordinary man and not bearing his lordship. It is to be told to one who serves and is devoted and has either austerity or intelligence.

sanskrit.deva:
य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥ ६८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati |
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ || 68 ||

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ idam paramam guhyam mat-bhakteṣu abhidhāsyati bhaktim mayi parām kṛtvā mām eva eṣyati asaṃśayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः इदम् परमम् गुह्यम् मत्-भक्तेषु अभिधास्यति भक्तिम् मयि पराम् कृत्वा माम् एव एष्यति असंशयः

translations.text: He who will teach this supreme secret among my devotees, having shown supreme devotion to me, will come to me alone, without doubt.

notes: Śaṅkara: this is the fruit for the one who hands the teaching on. The secret is this work, the dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna; to teach it is to establish it in text and meaning, as the Lord did in Arjuna. Devotion is named again to show that by devotion alone one becomes fit to receive it. He teaches thinking ‘I am serving the Lord, the supreme teacher’. He reads imam for idam.

sanskrit.deva:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥ ६९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ |
bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi || 69 ||

lines.iast: bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
lines.deva: भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि

padaccheda.iast: na ca tasmāt manuṣyeṣu kaścit me priya-kṛttamaḥ bhavitā na ca me tasmāt anyaḥ priyataraḥ bhuvi
padaccheda.deva: न च तस्मात् मनुष्येषु कश्चित् मे प्रिय-कृत्तमः भविता न च मे तस्मात् अन्यः प्रियतरः भुवि

translations.text: There is no one among men who does what is dearer to me than he; nor will there be another on earth dearer to me than he.

notes: Śaṅkara: than the one who hands on the teaching; none among those now living, and none in time to come.

sanskrit.deva:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥ ७० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ || 70 ||

lines.iast: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ
lines.deva: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः

padaccheda.iast: adhyeṣyate ca yaḥ imam dharmyam saṃvādam āvayoḥ jñāna-yajñena tena aham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ
padaccheda.deva: अध्येष्यते च यः इमम् धर्म्यम् संवादम् आवयोः ज्ञान-यज्ञेन तेन अहम् इष्टः स्याम् इति मे मतिः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: And he who will study this dialogue of ours, which accords with dharma, by him I would be worshipped with the sacrifice of knowledge: such is my conviction.

notes: Śaṅkara: of the sacrifices, the ritual, the muttered, the whispered and the mental, the sacrifice of knowledge is the best because it is mental; so this praises the study of the Gītā. Or it states the fruit: it equals that of a sacrifice of knowledge directed to a deity.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभांल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ ७१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śraddhāvān anasūyaś ca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ |
so 'pi muktaḥ śubhāṃllokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām || 71 ||

lines.iast: śraddhāvān anasūyaś ca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ

padaccheda.iast: śraddhāvān anasūyaḥ ca śṛṇuyāt api yaḥ naraḥ saḥ api muktaḥ śubhān lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya-karmaṇām
padaccheda.deva: श्रद्धावान् अनसूयः च शृणुयात् अपि यः नरः सः अपि मुक्तः शुभान् लोकान् प्राप्नुयात् पुण्य-कर्मणाम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: And the man who, full of faith and free from cavil, merely hears it, he too, freed, would attain the happy worlds of those of meritorious deeds.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘merely’: how much more one who knows its meaning. Freed: from sin. Those of meritorious deeds are performers of the Agnihotra and the like.

sanskrit.deva:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनंजय ॥ ७२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā |
kaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanaṃjaya || 72 ||

padaccheda.iast: kaccit etat śrutam pārtha tvayā eka-agreṇa cetasā kaccit ajñāna-saṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ te dhanaṃjaya
padaccheda.deva: कच्चित् एतत् श्रुतम् पार्थ त्वया एक-अग्रेण चेतसा कच्चित् अज्ञान-संमोहः प्रनष्टः ते धनंजय

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Has this been heard by you, O Pārtha, with a one-pointed mind? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed, O winner of wealth?

notes: Śaṅkara: he asks in order to know whether the pupil has grasped the teaching, meaning to teach it again by other means if he has not. This shows the dharma of a teacher: to take further pains until the pupil has reached his end.

sanskrit.deva:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसंदेहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥ ७३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta |
sthito 'smi gatasaṃdehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava || 73 ||

padaccheda.iast: naṣṭaḥ mohaḥ smṛtiḥ labdhā tvat-prasādāt mayā acyuta sthitaḥ asmi gata-saṃdehaḥ kariṣye vacanam tava
padaccheda.deva: नष्टः मोहः स्मृतिः लब्धा त्वत्-प्रसादात् मया अच्युत स्थितः अस्मि गत-संदेहः करिष्ये वचनम् तव

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle f. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed and memory has been gained by me through your grace, O Acyuta. I stand firm, with doubts gone; I shall do your word.

notes: Śaṅkara: delusion, born of ignorance, is the cause of all the evil of the cycle of birth and death, hard to cross like the sea. The memory is of the truth of the Self; on gaining it all the knots of the heart are loosed. This answer shows that the fruit of knowing the whole teaching is just this: the end of delusion and the gaining of the memory of the Self. ‘I stand in your command; by your grace I have reached my end; nothing remains for me to do.’

sanskrit.deva:
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥ ७४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ |
saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam || 74 ||

padaccheda.iast: iti aham vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahā-ātmanaḥ saṃvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutam roma-harṣaṇam
padaccheda.deva: इति अहम् वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महा-आत्मनः संवादम् इमम् अश्रौषम् अद्भुतम् रोम-हर्षणम्

words.meaning: that makes the hair stand on end

translations.text: Saṃjaya said: Thus I heard this wonderful dialogue of Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha, which makes the hair stand on end.

notes: Śaṅkara: the teaching is complete; Saṃjaya now speaks to show its link with the story.

sanskrit.deva:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥ ७५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ param |
yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam || 75 ||

padaccheda.iast: vyāsa-prasādāt śrutavān etat guhyam aham param yogam yoga-īśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam
padaccheda.deva: व्यास-प्रसादात् श्रुतवान् एतत् गुह्यम् अहम् परम् योगम् योग-ईश्वरात् कृष्णात् साक्षात् कथयतः स्वयम्

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: By the grace of Vyāsa I heard this supreme secret, this yoga, directly from Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga, as he himself declared it.

notes: Śaṅkara: by Vyāsa's grace he had gained divine sight. The work is called yoga because yoga is its purpose; or the dialogue is itself yoga. ‘Directly’: not by hearsay. He reads imaṃ guhyatamaṃ param, ‘this most secret, supreme’.

sanskrit.deva:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ७६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam |
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ || 76 ||

padaccheda.iast: rājan saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādam imam adbhutam keśava-arjunayoḥ puṇyam hṛṣyāmi ca muhuḥ muhuḥ
padaccheda.deva: राजन् संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादम् इमम् अद्भुतम् केशव-अर्जुनयोः पुण्यम् हृष्यामि च मुहुः मुहुः

translations.text: O king, remembering again and again this wonderful and holy dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

notes: Śaṅkara: the king is Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Holy: it removes sin even by being heard.

sanskrit.deva:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान्राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥ ७७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahānrājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ || 77 ||

lines.iast: vismayo me mahānrājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
lines.deva: विस्मयो मे महान्राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः

padaccheda.iast: tat ca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpam ati-adbhutam hareḥ vismayaḥ me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तत् च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपम् अति-अद्भुतम् हरेः विस्मयः मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः

translations.text: And remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, great is my wonder, O king, and I rejoice again and again.

notes: Śaṅkara: the form is the form of the universe (adhyāya 11).

sanskrit.deva:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥ ७८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama || 78 ||

lines.iast: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ
lines.deva: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः

padaccheda.iast: yatra yoga-īśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ yatra pārthaḥ dhanuḥ-dharaḥ tatra śrīḥ vijayaḥ bhūtiḥ dhruvā nītiḥ matiḥ mama
padaccheda.deva: यत्र योग-ईश्वरः कृष्णः यत्र पार्थः धनुः-धरः तत्र श्रीः विजयः भूतिः ध्रुवा नीतिः मतिः मम

translations.text: Where Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga, is, and where Pārtha, the bearer of the bow, is, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and unfailing right conduct: such is my conviction.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘where’: on whichever side. He is the Lord of all yogas, since the seed of all yoga springs from him. The bow is Gāṇḍīva. bhūti is the further growth of fortune.
